text:
Priya (AM): FYI we kicked off a POC with Bankly. They need an EU-only proof-of-concept for compliance reviewers. Quick asks: list of subprocessors, whether any inference traffic can egress outside EU, and a short config we can hand them showing pinned routing + fail behavior.
Diego (Solutions): Ok. Short answer: hosted endpoints can be region-specific. For strict EU-only we provide a routing policy that pins to eu-central / eu-west and can be configured to not fall back. We should show both options (strict vs standby) so legal can sign off.
Diego (Solutions): Can you confirm expected traffic profile? qps, avg tokens per request? helps estimate cost uplift.
Priya (AM): They expect <30 r/s steady, spikes to ~60 r/s for batch tests. Avg payload ~150 tokens. No BYOK for POC.
Nora (Legal): I'll prepare the subproc inventory. Note: we must explicitly call out any third-party telemetry/monitoring providers and the control plane location for routing decisions. If control-plane operational metadata leaves EU, we should put that in the compliance note.
Kai (Infra): Technical note: there are three places to call out: (1) data plane (request payloads) — we can guarantee they stay in EU regions if pinned; (2) edge/cache replication — small KV prefixes may be replicated across regional caches in EU-only setup, not outside EU; (3) control plane (metrics, routing health) — currently hosted in us-central, minimal telemetry may cross border. We can add an option to route control-plane endpoints to our EU control-plane for the customer but that's an enterprise-only change.
Diego (Solutions): Sample routing snippet for the POC (they like config examples):
```yaml
service:routing
geo_pin:
  regions: [eu-central-1, eu-west-1]
  require_capacity: true    # reject requests if pinned regions are out of capacity
  fallback: none            # explicit: no cross-region fallback
  cache_policy: regional
  telemetry_scope: minimal
```
Diego (Solutions): Explain: require_capacity=true => we return 429/503 when pinned regions are saturated. That looks good for auditors.
Priya (AM): Bankly also asked whether audit logs and request latencies are stored in EU. Is that something we can guarantee?
Kai (Infra): Audit logs for inference requests (payload hashes, timestamps, request IDs) can be configured to remain in EU for retention windows. Full payload retention is governed by the customer's retention policy; we can enable "payload not stored" for the POC or store in EU-only bucket for 90 days.
Nora (Legal): Perfect. Please put that in writing: "Audit logs and stored request artefacts for this POC will reside in EU-only storage (customer bucket) for 90 days unless otherwise requested." I'll include that in the SOW.
Priya (AM): They want the subproc CSV + a short para about telemetry by EOD tomorrow for their compliance team. Can we hit that?
Kai (Infra): I can deliver a network-path diagram + short note on cache behavior and cost delta by EOD. Cost uplift estimate for pinned routing (less bin-packing, regional waste): ~14% (ballpark for their qps/size).
Diego (Solutions): I'll package the YAML runbook + example curl and a short test harness for perf testing. Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://eu-central.api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" -H "X-Redwood-Routing: geo_pin=eu-central-1" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
Priya (AM): Good. Nora, will legal be ok with the control-plane note that Kai mentioned (us-central telemetry) if we explicitly say it's minimal and covered by DPA?
Nora (Legal): Yes but draft language should be explicit: "Control-plane operational metadata (routing health, metrics and anonymized telemetry) may be processed by our control plane hosted in the US; no customer payloads or PII are sent outside the EU as part of this telemetry. We will limit telemetry to routing/health metrics and request hashes." I'll prep that paragraph and the CSV.
comms-bot: Ticket created: PRESALES-8892. Owner: Kai (Infra). SLA: 48h.
Diego (Solutions): One operational caveat: if we set require_capacity=true, clients should implement retry/backoff logic. For the POC we should offer guidance: try 3 retries with exponential backoff and fall back to queueing tests.
Priya (AM): POC timeline: Bankly wants to run tests on Mon-Wed. We need all docs by Friday EOD. Confirm?
Kai (Infra): Friday EOD for docs is fine. I'll attach a network path PDF and the cost uplift calc.
Nora (Legal): I'll upload subproc CSV + the compliance paragraph and add a short clause for the SOW that the customer accepts fail-closed behavior for the POC.
Priya (AM): One more ask: can we provide a short line item for pricing impact for the POC showing assumed costs and the uplift? That helps procurement.
Kai (Infra): I'll produce a simple table (in the doc) showing baseline cost vs pinned routing cost (approx +14%).
Diego (Solutions): I'll assemble final zip: runbook (yaml + curl), perf harness, latency expectations, sample SOW language from Legal, subproc list, and network path diagram.
Priya (AM): Amazing. I'll send the package to Bankly and request a signed riser SOW accepting the EU-only/fail-closed configuration. Will update when signed. :white_check_mark:
